cases.name: Citizens United v. Federal Election Commission

components.decision: The Court invalidated restrictions on independent corporate and union election spending.
components.scope: Independent expenditures differ from donations directly to candidates; the ruling did not legalize unrestricted direct corporate donations.
components.survey_fit: The survey contrasts contribution limits with freedom to support campaigns. It does not isolate independent expenditures; no agreement rate with the holding can be calculated.

components.decision: The Court upheld the challenged disclosure and disclaimer requirements.
components.scope: This separate part of the decision prevents treating the entire judgment as eliminating campaign-finance regulation.
components.survey_fit: No earlier question about these disclosure requirements is included; leave this component unscored.

components.decision: The Court struck down the total a donor could contribute across candidates and committees.
components.scope: Per-recipient base limits were not struck down. Four justices joined Roberts’s reasoning; Thomas supplied the fifth vote with a separate rationale.
components.locator: Roberts opinion, Parts II–IV; Thomas concurrence.
components.survey_fit: The poll addresses candidate fundraising and spending, not the aggregate donor cap. This is broad regulatory context and a weak match to the legal question.
